Hi all — thanks for the screenshot, Liam. Quick diagnostics and fix:

1) What likely happened: a forwarded invite (or an invite created without explicit TZ info) can be interpreted as "floating" in some clients — the numeric time stays the same but the timezone context is lost. When the event includes a TZ (e.g., TZID=Europe/Dublin in the .ics), clients reliably map the time.
2) Google Calendar sometimes shows the event details correctly (11:00 Europe/Dublin) but places the block in the grid using the viewer's local timezone offset if the original invite used a floating time. That explains the 10:00 visual block for you.

Fix options we've used successfully:
- I created a fresh invite from Marissa's calendar where the event timezone is explicitly set to Europe/Dublin. I exported and attached the .ics (updated_invite.ics) and also re-sent the invite from marissa_cole@redwood.ai (so the organizer and TZ metadata are consistent).
- Recipients should accept the most recent invite and, if using Google Calendar, open the event and check "Event timezone" under Edit -> More options. If it shows two timezones, pick the explicit Europe/Dublin option.

Marissa — I already re-sent the invite from your account and attached the .ics. Liam/Emily please accept this one and delete any earlier forwarded copies.

Let me know if you still see mismatched times and we'll join a quick 5-min call to confirm.

Best,
